tasks.short: Check completed documents for spelling, grammar, punctuation and layout.

steps.what: Open the latest draft and its style instructions.
Read the copy and mark spelling, grammar and punctuation corrections.

loop.input: Review copy, style guide and issues remaining after configured spelling checks.
loop.output: Suggested corrections anchored to exact text spans, with reasons.
loop.check: Reject invalid spans and changes to protected names, numbers or references. A person checks meaning.
loop.stop: One pass per section and one repair attempt for invalid output; unresolved text stays unchanged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Configured checks handle routine errors. Context-dependent grammar and ambiguous phrasing need bounded language judgement.

steps.what: Check headings, spacing, page breaks and numbering against the required format.
Resolve wording queries with the document owner and record agreed corrections.

tasks.design: Configure spelling checks, styles and templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded language check proposes remaining corrections as tracked changes; the word processor reviews them and sends meaning queries through the {EMAIL}. Store the checked version and correction history in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Basic checks already existed. Inconsistent templates and context-dependent wording left substantial reading and correction work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document features handle routine checks. Coding assistance makes small validation tools cheaper, while bounded language checks can propose contextual edits.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist terminology, multilingual writing and changes that subtly alter meaning still need informed review. Complex tables and pagination need visual checking.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently cleaner sentence changes the author's intention or creates an unsupported commitment.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from correcting repeated errors to resolving meaning queries and improving reusable templates. Document owners retain authority over substantive wording and release.

reach.task: Prepare accessible meeting packs.
reach.learn: Document accessibility, heading structure, reading order and meeting deadlines.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling checks and document styles handle routine proofreading and formatting.
CHILI GraFx supports governed layout templates; this supports template-based production, not semantic proofreading accuracy.
GDPR applies to personal data in documents. Consultation requirements for changed working practices depend on national rules.

assumptions: Most work arrives as editable documents in the {DOCS}.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The document-heavy prior fits this task; contextual corrections retain review.
The solution checks documents and does not publish them.
unknowns: Languages, document volumes and specialist terminology.
Availability of approved templates and style guidance.
Permitted processing locations and access to confidential documents.
Applicable consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which configured checks preserve tracked changes and work across the required document formats?
How accurately can bounded checks detect errors without changing meaning in representative documents?
new_work: Review proposed corrections and resolve meaning queries.
Maintain approved terminology, templates and protected fields.
Sample accepted edits for meaning changes.
Maintain access controls and document retention settings.
tasks.statement: Check completed work for spelling, grammar, punctuation, and format.

tasks.short: Handle calls, route incoming mail, deliver physical items, run errands, and send occasional faxes.

steps.what: Answer incoming calls through {TELEPHONY} and establish the caller's need.
Consult the directory in {DOCS}, answer routine questions, or transfer calls through {TELEPHONY}.
Open authorised post and scan documents using scanning equipment in {OTHER}.
Read scanned mail in {DOCS} and incoming {EMAIL} to identify responsible teams.

loop.input: Unmatched scanned mail or incoming email, an allowed team list, and routing rules.
loop.output: Proposed team, supporting text, or an unresolved flag.
loop.check: Use direct identifiers first. Validate proposed teams against the directory and enforce restricted-mail rules.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per item; unreadable, ambiguous, or restricted items go to the office clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender and reference rules cannot route the remaining free-text requests reliably.

steps.what: Forward electronic mail through {EMAIL} or grant the receiving team access in {DOCS}.
Deliver physical originals and parcels to staff or collection points.
Complete local errands and obtain requested supplies or signatures.
Prepare the approved document and fax cover sheet in {DOCS}.
Send the fax using fax equipment in {OTHER} and check transmission confirmation.

tasks.design: Configure directory lookup and approved answers beside {TELEPHONY}, and collect scanned mail in {DOCS}. A {WORKFLOW} applies routing rules, uses a bounded classification loop for unmatched text, and presents proposed routes for release. Template generation and configured fax transmission reduce paperwork while calls, physical delivery, and errands remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling, calls, and digital routing were treated as one indivisible clerical duty. Unclear addresses and free-text mail resisted simple routing rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Directory controls and scanning workflows already cover routine preparation. A small classification loop can propose routes for residual text without controlling the whole job.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected callers, private correspondence, and physical errands remain varied. GDPR governs personal mail; the EU AI Act applies according to actual use, and national rules may require employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Understand an uncertain caller, recognise sensitive correspondence, and solve practical problems around the workplace.
tasks.altitude: The clerk keeps the live service role and spends less time reading routine mail for routing. Delegated rights can include resolving unassigned correspondence and correcting directory entries; confidential disclosure decisions stay with authorised owners.

reach.task: Resolve unassigned correspondence
reach.learn: Routing evidence, restricted-mail handling, and scan quality

reach.task: Identify recurring gaps in enquiry routing
reach.learn: Service ownership and aggregate queue analysis

evidence.claim: PostNL offers business-post scanning and conversion of forms into data.
Paperbox organises insurers' emails and attachments into case files; transfer to general office routing needs validation.
A Belfius case describes reduced mailroom administration, supporting partial automation rather than replacement of physical handling.
Live caller handling and physical errands remain substantial human work in this design.

assumptions: The steps represent separate call, mail, errand, and fax streams; they do not occur sequentially for every request.
Time shares are illustrative; fax work is occasional and may be absent.
This baseline includes scanning incoming post and forwarding electronic copies.
A usable staff directory and restricted-mail rules can be established.
The build covers one office and existing scanning equipment, without robotics or autonomous voice handling.
Consent and access effort includes mail permissions, data processing review, and applicable national employee consultation.

Whether post is currently scanned
Restricted correspondence categories
Availability of a maintained routing directory
Fax recipients that require the channel
Applicable consultation requirements
research_questions: How much mail routes correctly using exact references and sender rules alone?
Which ambiguous items require subject expertise rather than a team-directory lookup?
Can existing fax settings capture transmission evidence?
new_work: Review proposed routes and resolve unassigned items.
Maintain the directory and restricted-mail rules.
Check scan quality and routing errors.
Refresh approved answers when service ownership changes.
tasks.statement: Perform other clerical duties, such as answering telephone, sorting and distributing mail, running errands or sending faxes.

tasks.short: Gather source material, register it, resolve missing instructions, and arrange a typing packet.

steps.what: Gather drafts, corrected copies, recordings, and instructions from the requester.
Register the request and save identifiable source versions in the document store.
Read instructions, identify gaps, and arrange sources in the requested order.

loop.input: Registered source text, filenames, version metadata, and typing brief.
loop.output: Proposed source order, source references, and unresolved instructions.
loop.check: Require every source identifier exactly once; flag version conflicts; the word processor approves the order.
loop.stop: One proposal and one repair per packet; unresolved ordering or unreadable sources return to the word processor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata rules handle routine ordering, but handwritten corrections and free-text instructions can change source precedence.

steps.what: Resolve missing material and conflicting instructions with the requester.
Assemble the confirmed brief and ordered sources into a typing packet.

tasks.design: Configure intake from {EMAIL} into {DOCS}, with request identifiers, version tracking, and required fields in {WORKFLOW}. Rules assemble routine packets; a bounded model proposes ordering for ambiguous instructions, and the word processor approves that proposal. Confirmed instructions produce a linked typing packet automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material arrives in mixed formats, and source precedence often lives in informal instructions. Small intake volumes made bespoke integration hard to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake and versioning features cover routine work. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting them and building packet assembly; bounded text reading handles residual ambiguity.
tasks.still_hard: Illegible corrections, missing recordings, and contradictory instructions still need the requester. Access permissions must carry through to the assembled packet.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a seemingly minor correction changes the requester's intended meaning.

ambition.what: A submission-readiness check for occasional document requesters.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting files to resolving unclear briefs and improving submission quality. With delegated authority, the word processor can return incomplete requests before typing starts; content approval stays with the requester.

reach.task: Apply document classifications and retention labels to completed packets.
reach.learn: Learn version control, retention schedules, and permission inheritance.

evidence.claim: Configured intake, version registration, and deterministic packet assembly are feasible without an autonomous agent.
Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files; this supports intake feasibility, not a measured result for typing packets.

assumptions: Most sources are digital documents or recordings; physical originals are an exception.
Requests recur often enough to reuse a short intake form and packet structure.
Time shares are estimates for active work, excluding waits for requester replies.
Access review includes GDPR requirements and any employee consultation required by national rules; no individual productivity scoring is proposed.
unknowns: Available intake, versioning, and permission features in the current {DOCS}.
Frequency of physical originals, conflicting versions, and missing instructions.
Whether the word processor may return incomplete requests.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approved processing locations.
research_questions: How accurately can simple metadata rules order a representative sample before adding a model?
Which ambiguity types still require source-by-source review?
new_work: Review proposed ordering and resolve flagged version conflicts.
Maintain intake fields, packet templates, and source-access mappings.
Sample completed packets for omitted sources and incorrect precedence.
tasks.statement: Gather, register, and arrange the material to be typed, following instructions.

tasks.short: Produce typed correspondence and reports from drafts, corrections, recordings and previous versions.

steps.what: Collect source material, the previous version and document instructions.
Ask the document owner about unclear wording or conflicting instructions.
Copy reusable text and enter explicit corrections from previous versions.
Transcribe remaining handwritten text, recordings or dictation into the draft.

loop.input: Untranscribed source pages or audio segments, with explicit corrections and a controlled terminology list.
loop.output: Source-aligned text with page or time references and marked uncertain passages.
loop.check: Check segment coverage, source alignment and unexplained repetition; a person checks uncertainty, names, numbers and instructions against the source.
loop.stop: At most two passes per page or audio segment and a fixed document processing budget; unresolved passages go to manual transcription.
loop.why_not_simpler: Direct text reuse and explicit edit rules cannot interpret handwriting or speech. Use configured recognition first and restrict the loop to unresolved passages.

steps.what: Compare the draft with sources and correct transcription errors.
Approve the wording and intended use of the checked draft.
File the approved version and its source references.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} retains source versions while deterministic tools reuse existing text, apply explicit edits and generate the document. Configured recognition and a bounded extraction loop handle remaining handwriting or speech, with source-linked review and document-owner approval before the approved version is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed source formats, poor recordings and informal corrections made reliable conversion difficult. Earlier tools often separated recognition from revision and approval.
tasks.enabler_now: Recognition is readily available, while source alignment, document comparison and approval can be connected with small integrations. Better assembly reduces retyping even where recognition quality has not improved.
tasks.still_hard: Names, numbers, accents, overlapping speech and illegible handwriting remain costly to verify. Fluent text can conceal omissions or invented wording.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve the author's intended meaning without silently rewriting it, and recognise passages whose consequences warrant careful confirmation.

ambition.what: Provide reviewed dictation-to-document support for staff who struggle with written input.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving uncertain passages and helping authors express decisions clearly. The person can stop a draft with unresolved source conflicts; the author retains authority over its meaning and use.

reach.task: Turn dictated decisions into reviewed correspondence.
reach.learn: Learn audience requirements, confidentiality handling and decision-confirmation practices.

evidence.claim: Amberscript offers machine transcription and human-checked transcription.
A published study documents invented phrases in speech-to-text output, supporting source-based review.
Digital text reuse and explicit corrections can use deterministic processing before recognition is considered.

assumptions: The step shares represent the source mix across the workload; individual documents may skip reuse or transcription.
Sources may be processed for this purpose under an established GDPR basis.
The workflow prepares documents and does not make decisions about people.
The EU AI Act applies according to the system's intended use; ordinary transcription alone does not establish a high-risk employment use.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates; no vendor accuracy claim is used as a customer forecast.
unknowns: Which languages, recording conditions and handwriting styles occur?
What proportion of work already contains reusable digital text?
Are source recordings authorised, and what retention periods apply?
May source material leave the existing processing environment?
What employee consultation is required under national rules?

Does a bounded correction pass improve source fidelity enough to justify its cost?

Maintain terminology lists and extraction instructions.
Manage source access, retention and approved processing arrangements.
Sample apparently clean transcripts for hidden omissions or invented text.
Handle failed recognition and requests for author clarification.
tasks.statement: Type correspondence, reports, text and other written material from rough drafts, corrected copies, voice recordings, dictation, or previous versions, using a computer, word processor, or typewriter.

tasks.short: File completed documents, retrieve records, manage revisions, and remove records under retention rules.

steps.what: Collect completed documents from {EMAIL} and working folders in {DOCS}.
Choose document names, categories, and record references in {DOCS}.
Store documents in {DOCS}, checking location, permissions, and duplicate copies.
Search {DOCS} for requested records and provide document references.
Replace outdated copies and link approved revisions in {DOCS}.
Review retention dates and approve eligible document deletion in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure intake, required metadata, versioning, access groups, and retention queues in {DOCS}. Permission-filtered search lets authorised staff retrieve records directly, while a {WORKFLOW} approval releases eligible deletions after hold checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Folder conventions depended on memory. Final documents arrived without consistent references, and retention settings were not maintained.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes small intake adapters and migration checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy duplicates, unclear ownership, and conflicting retention instructions require people. GDPR obligations still apply; employee consultation depends on national rules and the proposed controls.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a document belongs to a sensitive case or must remain available despite routine retention dates.

ambition.what: Permission-controlled document retrieval for field staff

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving record exceptions and helping staff find authoritative material. They can correct routine metadata within delegated limits; access and disposal authority remain with record owners.

reach.task: Prepare a retention exception queue
reach.learn: Retention classes, legal holds, and disposal evidence

reach.task: Improve document retrieval for field staff
reach.learn: Access-group design and retrieval service measures

evidence.claim: Metadata rules, versioning, access groups, and retention queues can handle routine filing without a model.
GDPR applies to personal records; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and implementation.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative task-time estimates, not measured customer data.
Filing, retrieval, revision, and disposal are recurring branches rather than one sequence for every document.
Most new documents can inherit metadata from an intake form or source folder.
The target uses existing document capabilities before adding custom code.
Build ranges cover one repository and a limited legacy sample, not a full archive migration.
Consent and access effort includes permission review and applicable employee consultation; elapsed approval time may be longer.

Archive size and metadata quality

tasks.statement: File and store completed documents on computer hard drive or disk, or maintain a computer filing system to store, retrieve, update, and delete documents.

tasks.short: Print documents and make required paper copies.

steps.what: Make convenience copies for routine internal circulation using office printing equipment.
Set quantities, page ranges and finishing options for required paper copies.
Load paper or originals and run required jobs on office printing equipment.
Collect, inspect and assemble the required paper sets.

tasks.design: Replace convenience copies with permission-controlled access to the checked document in the {DOCS}. Configure print presets and secure release on office printing equipment in the {OTHER}. The word processor handles required paper, equipment exceptions and final inspection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recipients expected paper, and print requests arrived with inconsistent settings. Loading, collecting and inspecting paper remained physical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Document access controls, print presets and automatic finishing already exist. The main change is agreeing when digital circulation replaces paper.
tasks.still_hard: Originals, unusual stock, jams and mixed paper packs still require handling. Some recipients or processes require paper.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the finished pack is usable and resolve practical equipment or recipient needs.

ambition.what: Accessible digital document packs for remote staff.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer convenience-copy runs and more support for document access and print exceptions. Print preparation alone creates no new decision rights.

reach.task: Review shared printing capacity and recurring equipment faults.
reach.learn: Aggregate demand, equipment service arrangements and accessibility needs.

evidence.claim: Digital circulation, print presets and automatic finishing can reduce copying work; physical handling remains.
GDPR applies to personal data in printed and digital documents. Employee consultation depends on the change and national rules.

assumptions: Convenience-copy work is separable from required paper production.
The assumed 30% convenience-copy share needs measurement.
The low automation prior fits physical handling, but understates gains where paper circulation can disappear.
The {OTHER} slot represents office printing equipment and its print controls.
unknowns: Which paper copies recipients genuinely require.
Available secure release and finishing features.
Actual handling time, print volumes and equipment fault rates.
Whether remote staff can access accessible digital documents.
Local access approvals and consultation requirements under national rules.

Which digital pack format best preserves accessibility and stable page references?

Help recipients with document access.
Handle print failures and required paper exceptions.
Review aggregate print demand without introducing individual speed monitoring.
tasks.statement: Print and make copies of work.

tasks.short: Maintain records of completed typing work, document references, effort and outstanding corrections.

steps.what: Gather completed document references and assignment details.
Enter completion dates, document references, quantities and status in the work register.
Record effort and explain unusual work or unfinished corrections.
Reconcile missing or duplicate work records against document history.
Send a summary of completed work and outstanding corrections.

tasks.design: Completion events from the {DOCS} populate a configured work register in the {WORKFLOW}, removing separate gathering and re-entry. Rules reconcile document identifiers and status changes, while people declare effort and explain exceptions; the {WORKFLOW} produces an aggregate queue summary for the administrative supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document history and the work register were separate, and assignment identifiers were inconsistent. Effort and completion were often recorded together by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, event triggers and stable document identifiers can capture completion once. Small deterministic integrations can reconcile status without interpreting employee activity.
tasks.still_hard: A saved document is not necessarily completed work. Event timestamps cannot establish effort, and reopened assignments need clear counting rules.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why work took an unusual path and distinguish genuine completion from a file update.

ambition.what: Review queue priorities each day using overdue assignments and correction backlogs.

tasks.altitude: The person spends less time reconstructing activity and more time resolving stalled assignments. They gain authority to flag and propose daily priority changes; the administrative supervisor retains staffing and performance decisions.

reach.task: Adjust document-service capacity and priorities.
reach.learn: Learn queue ageing, service commitments and how to distinguish demand from rework.

evidence.claim: Completion metadata, duplicate checks and aggregate summaries can use configured workflows and deterministic rules.
In the Netherlands, per-clerk speed or touchless dashboards require works-council consent under the cited provision.
Document timestamps alone do not reliably measure human effort.

assumptions: A shared workbook is the baseline work register; customers already using a records app may need configuration only.
The document-heavy prior is adjusted because maintaining the record usually occurs in a register.
The register tracks assignments and declared effort; it does not infer working time from computer activity.
GDPR requirements apply to identifiable work records; national rules determine additional consultation requirements.
Build ranges are working-day estimates, and consultation lead time may exceed implementation time.

Are records used for billing, payroll, performance assessment or statutory evidence?
Can the {DOCS} emit completion events with stable assignment identifiers?
Which employee representatives, access owners and retention rules apply?

Which fields need personal declaration rather than automatic capture?

Review unmatched events, duplicates and reopened assignments.
Declare effort and explain unusual work.
Maintain access, retention and employee consultation arrangements.
Monitor failed event delivery and reconcile missed updates.

tasks.short: Calculate totals on financial forms, compare them with stated amounts, and resolve discrepancies.

steps.what: Read line amounts, quantities, rates, and stated totals from financial forms.

loop.input: Financial forms without usable structured fields.
loop.output: Line amounts, quantities, rates, currency, and stated totals with source locations.
loop.check: Validate field types, currency, decimal conventions, and line coverage; review uncertain fields against originals.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per form; unresolved fields go to manual entry before calculation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured inputs bypass extraction; remaining scanned or irregular forms require reading their layout and labels.

steps.what: Enter figures into calculation cells and compute subtotals, adjustments, and totals.
Compare calculated totals with the form and record differences.
Send discrepancies and supporting figures to the finance reviewer.
Decide whether the difference needs correction or reflects an authorised calculation rule.

tasks.design: Use structured fields from {ERP} or {PROCUREMENT} wherever available, eliminating document re-entry; apply a bounded extraction loop only to residual forms in {DOCS}. Configure arithmetic, currency, rounding, and comparison rules in {ERP}, with a controlled {SPREADSHEET} template where needed. Route differences through {WORKFLOW}, and require finance approval before corrections affect financial records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were trapped in documents, and calculation conventions differed between forms. Built-in validation was not consistently connected to incoming files.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured calculations already handle the arithmetic. Faster integration work and document extraction make it cheaper to connect residual forms to those controls.
tasks.still_hard: A mathematically correct total can still use the wrong rate, tax treatment, or underlying transaction. Irregular scans and inconsistent rounding rules need exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a typing or arithmetic error from a legitimate commercial adjustment.

ambition.what: A pre-submission arithmetic check for departmental requisitions.

tasks.altitude: Routine calculation time largely disappears, leaving source-quality exceptions and correction follow-up. The word processor can issue a documented arithmetic result but gains no payment or accounting-policy authority.

reach.task: Check requisitions for complete financial fields before routing them.
reach.learn: Learn decimal handling, rounding conventions, and the boundary between arithmetic checks and financial approval.

evidence.claim: Exact arithmetic and tolerance checks can use configured rules rather than model-generated calculations.
Rossum extracts, validates, and posts invoice data to finance systems; this supports the document-input component.
The Fugro vendor case reports invoice processing falling from two minutes to 35 seconds; this is not a forecast for this task.

assumptions: The representative current method is a controlled calculation workbook; calculators remain possible for occasional forms.
This task covers arithmetic validation, not approval of spending, tax treatment, or payments.
Forms already calculated and validated in a source system need no duplicate calculation.
Time shares cover a batch including discrepancy cases and finance review.
Access approval covers GDPR where forms contain personal data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Proportion of forms already available as structured fields.
Current calculation tools and duplication of existing system checks.
Approved rounding rules, currencies, tolerances, and correction authority.
Access to source-system validation and exception-routing features.
research_questions: Which duplicate checks can be removed because the source system already enforces them?
Can extraction detect omitted lines reliably enough on representative forms?
new_work: Review uncertain extracted fields and unresolved differences.
Maintain approved calculation rules and tolerance settings.
Check that source-format changes do not omit lines or alter decimal interpretation.
tasks.statement: Compute and verify totals on report forms, requisitions, or bills, using adding machine or calculator.

tasks.short: Collate report pages and attachments into complete, correctly ordered document sets.

steps.what: Collect report pages, attachments and assembly instructions.
Arrange pages and attachments in the required sequence.
Check completeness, page sequence and attachment versions.
Assemble paper sets and insert physical attachments where requested.
Save the checked document with its version and assembly reference.

tasks.design: A configured intake in the {DOCS} collects versioned sources and an assembly manifest. A deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} orders pages, checks counts and duplicates, and presents exceptions before saving the checked document in the {DOCS}; physical inserts remain a handling task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources arrived separately, naming was inconsistent, and assembly instructions were rarely captured as reusable rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls and inexpensive assembly scripts can handle repeatable packets. AI coding can reduce implementation effort without changing the underlying page-handling technology.
tasks.still_hard: A complete manifest can still describe the wrong source version. Unnumbered scans, foldouts and physical attachments require inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when a technically complete packet is inappropriate for its intended reader, and resolve conflicting source versions.

ambition.what: Offer a pre-meeting document-pack completeness check.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from page handling to resolving incomplete packets before deadlines. The person gains authority to return incomplete submissions against an agreed checklist, not to approve their substantive content.

reach.task: Prepare decision packs for project checkpoints.
reach.learn: Learn checkpoint requirements, document dependencies and submission cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Page assembly, manifest checks and versioned filing can use deterministic document processing.
Physical inserts and ambiguous versions limit fully unattended collation.

Most packets have an explicit page order or reusable section sequence.
The prior's large gathering share falls when assembly instructions identify source locations.

tasks.statement: Collate pages of reports and other documents.

tasks.short: Retrieve source material, sort text and numbers, merge documents, and verify the compiled result.

steps.what: Retrieve requested source documents and workbooks from {DOCS}.
Read source documents in {DOCS} and copy required passages and values.

loop.input: Residual source documents, requested fields, and a fixed output schema.
loop.output: Staged values or verbatim passages with document and page references; missing values explicitly flagged.
loop.check: Use direct field reads first. Check types, required fields, source references, and quoted text; reconcile numerical values before release.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved items enter the verification queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Residual documents place requested information in varied prose and layouts without stable field locations.

steps.what: Sort, standardise, and reconcile numerical rows in {SPREADSHEET}.
Merge passages, tables, and updated sections into a document in {DOCS}.
Compare the compiled draft with sources and resolve omissions or conflicting values.
Approve the compiled version and save it as current in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Read structured sources directly and use a bounded extraction loop only for residual documents from {DOCS}. Deterministic jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} sort and reconcile fields, then generate a draft in {DOCS} from a governed template. Source-linked exceptions support verification before a {WORKFLOW} approval makes the compilation current.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source layouts varied, and compilation rules were embedded in individual workbooks and personal habits. Reliable extraction and traceable verification required bespoke setup.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to implement mappings, validators, and document generators. Bounded extraction can handle some layout variation while deterministic checks control assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting sources and undocumented meanings cannot be resolved by formatting rules. Tables, units, dates, and missing pages need careful validation; automated extraction can still produce plausible errors.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve which source is authoritative and recognise when a technically consistent compilation misrepresents the underlying material.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week investigating discrepancies and improving compilation quality. They can resolve documented source-precedence cases within delegated limits; document owners approve substantive interpretation and release.

reach.learn: Schema validation, provenance, and correction trails

reach.task: Explain changes between compilation versions
reach.learn: Reconciliation, source precedence, and concise variance commentary

Doxis reads invoices, receipts, and email attachments into fields; broader document extraction requires separate validation.
Deterministic sorting, reconciliation, and document assembly can replace repeated manual compilation.
A documented spreadsheet row-limit failure supports explicit completeness and row-count checks.

tasks.statement: Electronically sort and compile text and numerical data, retrieving, updating, and merging documents as required.

tasks.short: Reformat documents by applying styles and moving paragraphs or columns to the requested layout.

steps.what: Read the document and requested layout changes.
Apply paragraph styles, margins, headings and column settings.
Move specified paragraphs, tables and columns into their required positions.
Inspect page breaks, reading order, tables and content preservation.
Save the checked version and return its reference.

tasks.design: Governed templates in the {DOCS} apply standard styles, while a deterministic generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} moves explicitly identified content blocks. Content comparisons and rendered previews support a focused layout review before the checked version is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents relied on manual spacing and inconsistent styles. Layout requests often referred to positions rather than stable section identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Template configuration handles routine formatting, and small scripts can preserve and relocate structured content. AI coding makes format adapters cheaper to build, although unusual layouts still need review.
tasks.still_hard: Floating objects, damaged files, complex tables and vague instructions can defeat reliable transformations. Automated content checks do not establish good visual hierarchy.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret the reader's needs and choose a clear layout when instructions allow several reasonable arrangements.
tasks.altitude: The person spends more time reviewing difficult layouts and improving templates. They can select approved layout patterns and reject unclear instructions; document owners retain content decisions.

reach.task: Maintain accessible templates for recurring reports and correspondence.
reach.learn: Learn heading structure, reading order, table accessibility and template change control.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx supports governed template-based layout generation; this supports the template approach, not arbitrary document conversion.
Styles, explicit block moves and content comparisons can be implemented without a model loop.

assumptions: Routine requests identify the content to move; ambiguous requests remain human work.
Source documents usually contain editable text rather than scans.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The high automation prior is moderated by rendered-layout inspection and irregular source files.
unknowns: Which document formats and layout features occur most often?
Are approved templates and stable section identifiers available?
Which accessibility requirements apply to the outputs?
What access and consultation are required under national rules?
research_questions: Which layout transformations preserve text, tables, links and reading order reliably?
How often do explicit transformation rules cover incoming requests without interpretation?
new_work: Maintain templates and supported transformation rules.
Review visual previews and content differences.
Handle unsupported objects and ambiguous move instructions.
Retest representative documents after rendering or template changes.
tasks.statement: Reformat documents, moving paragraphs or columns.

tasks.short: Find specified text in stored documents and apply controlled replacements.

steps.what: Confirm replacement text and document scope with the document owner.
Search the selected documents and inspect matching text.
Replace approved matches in working copies.
Check changed passages and save the revised version.

tasks.design: Use configured search, replacement, comparison and version history in the {DOCS}. Capture literal text, scope and exclusions before producing a revised draft. The word processor reviews changed passages before saving the checked version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Search and replace already existed. Ambiguous instructions, inconsistent files and fear of unintended replacements limited bulk use.
tasks.enabler_now: No model breakthrough is needed. Existing comparison and version controls make reversible changes practical when the replacement specification is explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Identical text can have different meanings in different passages. Scanned files, protected sections and embedded objects may need separate handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a match that should remain unchanged because its context differs from the request.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated searching to defining safe change scopes and checking exceptions. Routine replacements can proceed within an agreed remit; substantive wording decisions stay with the document owner.

reach.task: Identify authoritative document versions and superseded copies.
reach.learn: Version control, retention schedules and document ownership.

evidence.claim: Literal search, replacement, document comparison and version history are established deterministic capabilities.
Context-sensitive replacements need scope controls and review even when matching is deterministic.

assumptions: Most requests specify literal text changes in editable documents.
The document-heavy prior fits; the main opportunity is configuring existing capabilities.
No semantic search or autonomous agent is required.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Run cost excludes existing {DOCS} licensing and staff upkeep.
unknowns: Supported file formats and available comparison features.
Frequency of changes spanning multiple files.
Permissions to edit authoritative documents.
Prevalence of protected sections, scans and embedded objects.
Access approval lead times and any consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Do configured searches include headers, footnotes, tables and hidden text?
Can existing batch tools preserve formatting and produce complete change records?
new_work: Maintain replacement specifications and exclusions.
Review contextual exceptions and changed passages.
Check that version recovery works.
Maintain terminology lists for the optional consistency service.
tasks.statement: Search for specific sets of stored, typed characters to make changes.

tasks.short: Apply document styles, page layouts, spacing and formatting requirements.

steps.what: Inspect the draft and identify the required document template.
Apply styles, margins, headings, spacing, headers and footers.
Check page breaks, tables, numbering and visual consistency.
Save the checked version in the correct document location.

tasks.design: Governed templates in the {DOCS} apply styles and layout settings while preserving the source version. A deterministic checker renders the result, flags layout failures and presents a proof for review before the checked version is filed in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local formatting habits, inconsistent templates and pasted direct formatting made reliable reuse difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Styles and templates already solve much of the task. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of adding document checks and handling recurring file variations.
tasks.still_hard: Complex tables, embedded objects, accessibility and unusual pagination still need visual inspection. Template maintenance can cost more than generation for rare document types.
tasks.human_edge: Judge readability and whether the layout gives the right emphasis to the content.

ambition.what: An accessible document preparation service for teams without publishing support.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated formatting to reviewing difficult layouts and improving document templates. Delegated approval of standard layout exceptions can expand; approval of document content does not change.

reach.task: Prepare accessible reports and correspondence.
reach.learn: Semantic styles, accessible tables, reading order and document quality checks.

evidence.claim: Governed template filling is available today; this supports the building block, not a claim about office-document compatibility.
Document styles, template settings and deterministic checks can handle routine formatting without a model.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
A small set of recurring document types accounts for much of the work.
The review gate approves formatting; any required content approval remains separate.
Build ranges cover an initial template family and include access and applicable national consultation.
GDPR applies to document contents; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI functionality actually introduced.
unknowns: Which file formats and document templates dominate?
How much direct formatting and embedded content appears?
Which accessibility and house-style requirements apply?
Who may approve layout exceptions?
research_questions: Which formatting defects can be detected reliably before visual review?
Can native template settings handle the common documents without a custom generator?
new_work: Maintain approved templates and version compatibility.
Review flagged pagination, table and accessibility problems.
Check representative documents after template changes.
tasks.statement: Adjust settings for format, page layout, line spacing, and other style requirements.

tasks.short: Prepare addressed envelopes or labels from approved recipient details.

steps.what: Retrieve approved recipient names and postal addresses.
Type recipient details into envelope or label layouts.
Check names, addresses, duplicates and label alignment.
Load envelopes or label stock and print using office printing equipment.

tasks.design: Use an approved export from the {CRM} to populate mail-merge templates in the {DOCS}. Deterministic checks flag missing fields, duplicate records and layout overflow; the word processor resolves exceptions and approves the labels. Print through office printing equipment in the {OTHER}, then hand over to the mail clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mail merge already existed, but recipient exports and label layouts were poorly connected. Address exceptions encouraged manual typing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured exports and mail merge remove re-keying. Small deterministic checks are inexpensive to build and do not need a model.
tasks.still_hard: Complete fields do not prove that an address is current or deliverable. International formats, stale records and unusual stock remain exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve uncertain recipient details with the record owner and recognise a plausible but incorrect address.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less address typing and more source-data correction and print exception handling. Recipient selection and mailing authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Correct verified postal-address errors in recipient records.
reach.learn: Source verification, duplicate handling and authorised record correction.

evidence.claim: Mail merge can generate envelopes and labels directly from structured recipient lists without language models.
CHILI GraFx demonstrates governed template filling; ordinary envelope preparation may need only existing mail merge.
GDPR applies to recipient names and addresses, including exported mailing lists.

assumptions: This baseline uses recipient records in the {CRM}; staff mailings may instead use the {HCM}.
Recipient selection is approved before label preparation.
The low automation prior understates deterministic gains in address typing; physical printing remains partly manual.
The {OTHER} slot represents office printing equipment.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
unknowns: Actual address sources and export permissions.
Mailing volumes, destination countries and address quality.
Installed mail-merge and printing capabilities.
Required retention periods for recipient exports.
Applicable consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Which destination-specific formatting rules can be checked without an external address service?
Can configured exports supply only approved recipients and necessary address fields?
new_work: Review missing fields, duplicates and layout exceptions.
Return uncertain addresses to the record owner.
Maintain label templates and export mappings.
Delete temporary recipient exports under the agreed retention rules.
tasks.statement: Address envelopes or prepare envelope labels, using typewriter or computer.

tasks.short: Keep shared printers and office equipment supplied and ready for use.

steps.what: Inspect printer {OTHER} status and check paper and toner levels.
Retrieve compatible paper, cartridges or other consumables from storage.
Refill printer {OTHER} paper and replace depleted consumables.
Run a printer {OTHER} test and check output quality.
Update the stock workbook and identify replenishment needs.

tasks.design: Configure device-management alerts in the {OTHER} and route supply needs through the {WORKFLOW}. A small stock register in the {WORKFLOW} replaces the {SPREADSHEET}, records confirmed replacements and flags replenishment needs; retrieving supplies, replacing them and checking print quality remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical replacement cannot be automated with office software. Status checks and stock updates often lacked a reliable connection to device events.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing device alerts can remove routine inspection where supported. AI-assisted coding makes a small stock register and alert connection inexpensive to build; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Device compatibility, inaccurate supply estimates and unrecorded stock movements limit automation. Physical faults and consumable replacement still require someone on site.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose visible print problems and restore equipment when remote status reports are misleading.
tasks.altitude: Routine status rounds shrink, leaving more time for physical replenishment and fault handling. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan consumable availability and coordinate equipment repairs.
reach.learn: Reorder thresholds, equipment compatibility and service escalation.

evidence.claim: Device alerts and threshold-based stock registers can automate checks and administrative follow-up.
Office software cannot replace physical loading, cartridge replacement or visual print inspection.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates.
Modern shared printers dominate; obsolete media handling is uncommon.
Supported devices expose usable supply alerts; unsupported devices retain manual checks.
Stock changes require confirmation of actual replacement, rather than inference from estimated toner levels.
Build ranges include device access and applicable consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies where device logs contain personal data; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI introduced.
unknowns: Which devices support usable alerts and test routines?
How are consumable compatibility and stock tracked today?
Who handles faults and approves purchases?
What proportion of work involves unsupported or specialist equipment?
research_questions: Can existing device settings provide reliable alerts without custom integration?
Does a quick replacement confirmation keep stock accurate enough for replenishment planning?
new_work: Maintain device-to-consumable mappings and reorder thresholds.
Handle stale alerts and unsupported devices.
Confirm replacements and reconcile occasional stock discrepancies.
tasks.statement: Operate and resupply printers and computers, changing print wheels or fluid cartridges, adding paper, and loading blank tapes, cards, or disks into equipment.

tasks.short: Prepare approved documents, send them electronically, and confirm delivery.

steps.what: Find the approved version in {DOCS} and prepare the required transmission format.
Enter recipients in {EMAIL} and check addresses, attachments, and sharing permissions.
Release the transmission through {EMAIL} or upload it to {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Check delivery notices and record transmission status in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure {DOCS} exports and a {WORKFLOW} dispatch form with recipient checks and a document-owner release action. Connect supported {EMAIL} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} delivery events to a transmission log, with failed or uncertain deliveries placed in an exception queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved versions, recipient details, and delivery evidence lived in separate places. Portal-specific steps made a common dispatch process harder to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export and approval settings handle the core process. Small deterministic connectors can link supported delivery events to document references.
tasks.still_hard: Recipient changes and unsupported portals need attention. A delivery notice may confirm technical delivery without proving that the recipient read or accepted the document.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the material is ready to release and whether the recipient should receive it.

ambition.what: Document dispatch status service for requesters

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles failed deliveries and unusual destinations instead of assembling each transmission. They gain delegated authority to resolve technical delivery issues, while document owners retain release decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate distribution of confidential meeting packs
reach.learn: Recipient verification, release timing, and restricted sharing

reach.task: Maintain a project deliverable transmission register
reach.learn: Document status, contractual delivery evidence, and acknowledgement rules

evidence.claim: Document exports, recipient checks, approval flows, and delivery-event logging can use deterministic technology.
The digest provides no documented case establishing savings for this exact dispatch workflow.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative and include document preparation, addressing, release, and tracking.
The mailbox share is higher than the prior because addressing and delivery tracking are central to this task.
The target supports one transmission format and one portal with a supported connector.
A document-owner gate applies to external release; internal distribution can use separately approved standing rules.
Consent and access effort covers destination access, sharing policy, and applicable national consultation.

Supported {PARTNER_PORTAL} interfaces
Who can approve each document class
Required delivery evidence and retention period
Whether recipients can use restricted document links
research_questions: Which deliveries can use existing sharing settings without a connector?
Which portal acknowledgements establish successful submission?

Maintain destination records and connector credentials.
Review release requests.
Test dispatch after portal or permission changes.
tasks.statement: Transmit work electronically to other locations.

tasks.short: Combine technical sources, reconcile figures, and prepare statistical tables and reports.

steps.what: Collect source reports and data exports for the requested reporting period.
Read technical headings and footnotes to identify definitions, units, and coverage.

loop.input: Technical source headings, footnotes, definitions, and reporting brief.
loop.output: Proposed definitions, units, periods, exclusions, and source references.
loop.check: Require source references for every definition; flag conflicting units and periods; the word processor approves the sheet.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per source bundle; unresolved meanings go to the technical reviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Known schemas use fixed mappings, but prose footnotes can change the meaning or coverage of a column.

steps.what: Combine figures, align categories, and reconcile totals across sources.
Plan table structure, headings, explanatory notes, and the order of technical material.
Type tables and assemble the report with consistent formatting and references.
Review technical meaning, unresolved differences, and suitability for release.

tasks.design: A pipeline on {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers approved exports and sources from {DOCS}, applies explicit mappings, and checks totals and coverage. A bounded model extracts definitions from unfamiliar footnotes for review; deterministic templates then generate tables and the report draft in {DOCS}. The technical reviewer approves meaning and release, while reusable views in {BI} support follow-up questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports mixed structured exports with technical documents, while category mappings and layout choices remained informal. Each recurring report looked too small to justify a dedicated pipeline.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes small importers, reconciliation checks, and document generators cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can propose footnote definitions without letting a model calculate or silently reconcile figures.
tasks.still_hard: Different sources may measure different populations or periods. Technical interpretation and changes to reporting definitions require domain expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when apparently comparable figures would produce a misleading table.

ambition.what: An on-demand departmental breakdown of an approved statistical report.

tasks.altitude: The week moves toward source reconciliation and explaining limitations, with less table typing. After training and delegation, the word processor can choose approved breakdowns and layouts; new measures and publication remain subject to technical approval.

reach.task: Prepare a comparable departmental breakdown and explain its limitations.
reach.learn: Learn metric definitions, joins, denominators, missing-data treatment, and cautious interpretation.

evidence.claim: Recurring tables can be generated deterministically from validated data and explicit layout specifications.
CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates; this supports template-driven production, not statistical reconciliation accuracy.
A governed pipeline can check row counts, joins, coverage, and totals before report generation.

assumptions: The role assembles descriptive reports from supplied sources rather than designing statistical research.
Some recurring source schemas and table layouts can be reused.
Time shares include technical review and exclude waiting for source owners.
Build estimates cover one recurring report family, not every technical report.
GDPR access and disclosure controls apply where sources contain personal data. EU AI Act duties depend on actual use; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Number and stability of source formats and reporting definitions.
Availability of approved exports and authoritative category mappings.
Presence of personal data, small groups, or restricted technical information.
Who can approve reconciliations, new breakdowns, and report release.
Existing {DATA_PLATFORM}, {BI}, and document-generation capabilities.
research_questions: How much apparent reconciliation work reflects genuinely incompatible definitions?
Which report layouts can become reusable specifications?
Can representative reports be reproduced with matching totals, footnotes, and source lineage?
new_work: Review extracted definitions and conflicting source coverage.
Maintain mappings, templates, and reconciliation rules when sources change.
Investigate failed joins, missing periods, and unexplained total movements.
Review new breakdowns for misleading comparisons or personal-data disclosure.
tasks.statement: Work with technical material, preparing statistical reports, planning and typing statistical tables, and combining and rearranging material from different sources.

tasks.short: Scan source material and produce checked, editable digital text.

steps.what: Sort paper originals and prepare pages for scanning.
Load the scanner {OTHER}, select settings and capture pages.
Run text recognition in capture software {OTHER}.
Compare recognized text with originals and correct recognition errors.

loop.input: Low-confidence text spans and their source page images.
loop.output: Proposed corrections with source locations and unresolved spans.
loop.check: Require a visible source location for every change; flag changed numbers and names for human comparison.
loop.stop: One proposal per flagged span and one validation retry, capped at 100 spans per document; unresolved or excess spans go to the typist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Recognition and dictionaries handle clean print; damaged characters and irregular layouts need source-aware interpretation.

steps.what: File the editable document with its source and reference details.

tasks.design: Use native digital originals when available; remaining paper passes through configured scanner and recognition profiles in the {OTHER}. A bounded model proposes corrections only for flagged spans, and the typist checks them before deterministic filing links the editable document to its source in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper handling remained physical, while inconsistent scan quality made text recognition unreliable. Manual comparison was the easiest way to catch omissions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured recognition handles clean print, and small source-linked model loops can assist with difficult spans. AI-assisted coding makes capture-to-filing integration cheaper.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile originals, handwriting, missing pages and exact reproduction of tables remain difficult. Sensitive documents require appropriate GDPR access, processing and retention controls.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when the source is ambiguous and ask its owner instead of inventing missing text.

ambition.what: A searchable legacy-document conversion service for departments with paper archives.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward difficult originals, source verification and batch quality checks. Physical handling remains, and authority over the meaning or retention of records does not change.

reach.task: Create searchable records while preserving source provenance.
reach.learn: Document indexing, retention schedules and capture-quality sampling.

evidence.claim: Business-post scanning and conversion of forms into data are available services.
Source-linked correction proposals can assist review, but exact editable-text fidelity requires local validation.
Physical paper preparation remains manual unless the input channel changes.

assumptions: Time shares describe paper-based cases; digital-source bypass is an additional opportunity, not counted in remaining percentages.
Most pages contain printed text; handwriting is an exception.
The model assists correction and never silently fills missing source content.
Build ranges include representative document testing, processing access and applicable consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies; EU AI Act obligations must be assessed for the actual recognition and model components.
unknowns: What share of originals already exists digitally?
Which languages, scan qualities and handwritten materials occur?
May source images be processed by the proposed model service?
Which records require complete comparison rather than sampled checks?
What scanner interfaces and capture licences are available?
research_questions: Does a bounded correction loop reduce review time without introducing unsupported text?
Which confidence thresholds reliably identify names, numbers and omitted text needing review?
new_work: Review proposed corrections and unresolved spans.
Maintain capture profiles and filing mappings.
Sample accepted pages for silent omissions.
Manage failed batches and source-to-document links.
tasks.statement: Use data entry devices, such as optical scanners, to input data into computers for revision or editing.

tasks.short: Arrange meetings, book locations, and maintain appointments.

steps.what: Read meeting requests and collect missing requirements.
Compare attendee availability and room capacity.
Resolve priority conflicts and select a meeting option.
Book the room and send invitations.
Handle declined invitations and agree revised arrangements.

tasks.design: A structured request in the {CALENDAR} replaces clarification messages and produces options using availability, room capacity and working hours. The organizer selects an option before the {CALENDAR} books and sends invitations; revised arrangements require approval before notices go out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incomplete requests and unshared external availability caused repeated coordination. Much of the required scheduling capability already existed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling settings and structured requests handle the routine path. AI-assisted coding makes small connector gaps cheaper to close; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: External availability, sensitive meeting titles and competing priorities still need careful handling. A free slot does not establish which meeting deserves priority.
tasks.human_edge: Understand relationships and urgency when moving one person's appointment affects others.

ambition.what: A weekly meeting-capacity clinic for teams with recurring scheduling conflicts.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving priority conflicts and advising organizers. The typist can gain delegated authority to choose routine slots within agreed working hours and attendee rules; priority decisions stay with organizers.

reach.task: Protect focus time while coordinating competing appointments.
reach.learn: Priority negotiation, calendar delegation and handling confidential appointments.

evidence.claim: Structured scheduling, availability checks and approval rules can use existing calendar capabilities.
The design requires configuration and bounded workflows rather than an autonomous agent.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Routine requests can move to structured intake; unusual requests remain exceptions.
Selecting a meeting explicitly authorizes its invitation and room booking.
The access estimate includes calendar delegation and any consultation required under national rules.
GDPR applies to calendar data; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI functionality actually introduced.
unknowns: Which scheduling and room-booking capabilities are enabled?
Can organizers and external attendees use structured availability requests?
Who may approve rescheduling and delegate routine booking authority?
What national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing scheduling settings cover the common requests without custom code?
Which request fields prevent the most clarification messages?
new_work: Maintain room capacities, working hours and booking permissions.
Resolve external availability and priority exceptions.
Review failed bookings and incorrect attendee selections.
tasks.statement: Manage schedules and set dates, times, and locations for meetings and appointments.
